derek-nutmeg.result: At a large size, I see more cat fur and whiskers. At a small size, I see more of Derek and his skin color. The eyes line up, but the human mouth and cat nose do not, so the large result still looks mixed.
derek-nutmeg.parameters: I choose sigma low = 10 and sigma high = 4. This removes fine detail from Derek and keeps enough cat fur and face shape. Sigma high = 2 makes the cat less clear. Gain = 1.2 strengthens the cat detail without changing the low-band average.
derek-nutmeg.color: I keep color in the low-frequency Derek image and make the cat detail grayscale. Skin color helps Derek show at small sizes. Color in both adds colored edges but does not fix the shape difference. High-only color is weak because the high-pass filter removes broad color areas.
derek-nutmeg.roles: After swapping, the small image looks more like a cat, with human eyes and teeth on top at larger sizes. I prefer the chosen version because the whiskers are clearer up close and Derek is clearer when small.

portraits.result: The large view shows more Trump detail around the eyes, forehead and mouth. The small view shows more of Obama and his smile. The switch is less clear than cat/owl because the mouths, hair and clothes do not all line up. Both people remain visible at some middle sizes.
portraits.parameters: I choose sigma low = 14 to remove more fine detail from Obama. Sigma high = 2 keeps only finer Trump detail than 3 or 4. I then choose gain = 2.4 to make that detail visible. This gives a clearer small-view switch than adding broader Trump shapes.
portraits.color: I choose grayscale. Color in the low band makes Obama stay too visible in the large image. High-only color has little effect. Color in both keeps the same broad color bias and adds colored edges. Grayscale makes the change depend more on shape and image size.
portraits.roles: Swapping makes Trump clearer in the small view and adds Obama eyes and teeth up close. Both versions show the mouth mismatch. I keep the selected version as an imperfect example of the identity change.

cat-owl.result: This is my favorite. At a large size, I see the owl beak, eye rims and feathers. At a small size, I see more of the cat nose, warm face and eye shape. The change is clearer than cat/tiger. A faint cat mouth is still visible near the beak.
cat-owl.parameters: I keep sigma low = 10 and sigma high = 2. This keeps fine owl detail while letting the cat show when small. I try gains 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 and 2, then choose 1.5. It makes the owl clearer than gain 1, while larger gains look too harsh. This adds 50% more high-band strength without changing its cutoff. The cutoff comparison also uses gain 1.5.
cat-owl.color: I choose cat color in the low band and grayscale owl detail. The warm color helps the small view look like a cat. Color in both can add colored edges around the eyes and feathers. High-only color loses the broad cat color. All four versions use gain 1.5 and the same alignment and filter sizes.
cat-owl.roles: With the owl in the low band, its broad face and beak stay visible when small. The cat detail does not replace it clearly. Keeping cat in the low band and owl in the high band gives the clearer large-owl/small-cat change.
